title: LSO Paralegal Ethics & Professional Responsibilities Practice Test 1 - Ethics & Professional Responsibilities - Communication with a Represented Party
exam: LSO Paralegal Ethics & Professional Responsibilities Practice Test 1
subject: Ethics & Professional Responsibilities

questions.q: A paralegal needs to formally serve a Plaintiff's Claim on the opposing party, who the paralegal knows is represented by a lawyer. The paralegal's process server hands the document directly to the opposing party. Does this constitute an ethical breach of communicating with a represented person?
options: Yes, formal service must always be directed only to the legal representative.
No, the rule against communicating with a represented party provides an exception for the formal service of documents.
Yes, unless the process server is also a licensed paralegal.
No, because the Plaintiff's Claim is a public document.
questions.explain: Rule 7.02 prohibits communication regarding the matter with a represented person without their representative's consent. However, the rule explicitly provides exceptions, one of which is that it does not prevent a paralegal from serving a formal legal document directly on a represented person.
